title: Kaleidoscope round
subtitle: A circular motif with eight coloured fan sections, one colour per section
excerpt: Eight fan sections each worked in a different colour give the kaleidoscope round its fractured glass-window appearance. Each colour works just one section and fastens off; the sections sit side by side with no colour blending. Eight colours in rotation produce a vivid circular tile with a dc border round in a neutral.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), multi-colour circular chapter (Internet Archive). Multi-section colour work in circular motifs was a well-established Victorian craft technique.
heroPrompt: A kaleidoscope crochet round motif in eight distinct vivid colours on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Eight coloured fan sections radiating from the centre, separated by a cream dc border, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished kaleidoscope round measures 12 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Kaleidoscope round
chartDefinition.caption: Eight sections, each in a different colour. Each section: 5 tr into a ch-2 sp from the foundation round. Border round in neutral.

glossaryTerms.definition: A motif that uses a different colour in each section, allowing yarn scraps of any length to be used up. Each section needs only enough yarn to complete one set of stitches.

content.text: : each of the eight fan sections uses a different colour, fastened off independently. This makes it useful for using up small yarn remnants where there is not enough of any single colour for a full motif.

Work the foundation round in a neutral to set the eight section spaces. Join each section colour separately, work the fan, fasten off, and weave in the end before starting the next section. The neutral border round joins all sections at their outer edges into a single motif.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 2 g each of 8 colours plus 4 g neutral for the border. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle for weaving ends.

content.text: Magic ring. *Ch 2, sl st back into ring.* Rep 8 times. Pull ring closed. (8 ch-2 spaces radiating from the ring.)
Join colour 1 to the first ch-2 sp. 5 tr into the sp. Fasten off. Rep for each of the remaining 7 ch-2 spaces with a different colour. (8 × 5-tr fans.)
Join neutral to the top of the first fan. *5 dc across the fan top. Ch 1 (between fans).* Rep from * around all 8 fans. Sl st to join. Fasten off.
Work the bullion round for a single-colour circular motif where the texture comes from the stitch structure rather than from colour sections.
